items.title: George "Pops" Foster and Mugsy Spanier Interview, 1957-04-21
items.q: Did you get together and play a lot together? Oh, yes, we played every night in Chicago.

ctx.x: He's throwing another party when I come to Boston, wait till I come there. George, he's throwing a party when he's throwing a party. He's throwing a party at his house.

He was quite a pure player then. He was? He was really influenced by the piano. Yes. Oh, that shows on his records. On his piano things. Did he write most of his tunes on the piano? Oh, yes. Those are all original. To me, on the piano. No one knows what he really amounted to for your life today. Yeah. No one knows. It might have been greater than him. They'd write about you with body pooped out. I think he'd probably have gone to the piano. You think so? I think so. He would have left his chorus completely. Well,…

Pops, Faust and Muggsy, Spanier, April 21st, 1957, reel three. Did you like the way he played? Oh, yes, I liked the way he played. Did you get together and play a lot together? Oh, yes, we played every night in Chicago. In various clubs? Oh, yes. No, there was a round roll. Oh, there are. Then we'd go out together. We'd go out the south side. And I'd probably go there. We'd sit in there together. I wouldn't care to go. Rap could really play some blues on guitar, couldn't he, Pop? Yeah, that's why I... How good a…
